nodes.rationale: Intelligence does not become sovereignty until it can acquire durable, consequential agency.
nodes.statement: Algorithmic capability (A), strategic hardware (H), and power-conversion affordances (P) are related but distinct variables and should not be governed as though they always change together.
nodes.title: Separate capability, substrate, and power

nodes.rationale: This preserves learning and option value while retaining intervention points.
nodes.statement: The objective is to slow and condition the conversion of frontier intelligence into irreversible economic, political, military, and physical power, not to freeze intelligence as such.
nodes.title: Pace conversion into irreversible power

nodes.rationale: Discovering a capability should not automatically confer the right to deploy it.
nodes.statement: Research inside genuinely bounded environments may proceed under a different regime from public, commercial, military, governmental, or otherwise power-conferring use.
nodes.title: Govern bounded research and consequential use differently

nodes.rationale: Safety evidence becomes a condition of access to economic and strategic rents.
nodes.statement: Consequential use that materially exceeds the observable foreign public capability frontier requires an adversarial control and safety case.
nodes.title: Require adversarial assurance above the public frontier

nodes.rationale: A grand bargain is not a credible prerequisite for initial action.
nodes.statement: The regime should begin as a domestically justified institution that can operate without foreign agreement and later admit deeper reciprocal cooperation.
nodes.title: Start domestically and remain internationally extensible

nodes.rationale: Cooperation can occur through a precommitted policy rule rather than trust. Which releases count toward the reference frontier matters: if the releases of other participants count, k participants can take turns releasing a margin above each other and the reference rises at about k times that margin per release interval, faster with more participants; referencing only non-participants holds it to their pace (research_notes/frontier-router, arithmetic on assumed inputs, checked against a closed form, not empirical; proposed Q17 asks which rule to adopt). The editorial reference's H5 raised the same ratchet as a hypothesis; it is not yet a YAML node.
nodes.statement: Observable foreign public capability should alter the domestic safe-harbor frontier so that foreign restraint can be reciprocated without a treaty and foreign release cannot exploit unilateral domestic restraint indefinitely.
nodes.title: Make foreign public capability an automatic reciprocity input

nodes.rationale: Observable intermediate boundaries create chances to learn before failures become irreversible.
nodes.statement: Governance should maximize the interval between credible detection of a dangerous transition and the point at which humans can no longer respond effectively.
nodes.title: Maximize warning time

nodes.statement: A domestic compact governs transitions from bounded research into public, commercial, military, governmental, or other consequential use.
nodes.title: Capability Release Compact

nodes.statement: Qualified competitors receive controlled access sufficient to attack a frontier applicant's case; the government adjudicates and competitors do not hold a veto.
nodes.title: Rival laboratories provide the technical attack surface

nodes.statement: Because above-frontier monetization depends on passing hostile review, controllability becomes a production input rather than only a cost.
nodes.title: Safety becomes part of the profit function

nodes.statement: Reversibility depends on both the quantity of strategic hardware and the degree to which civilian society depends on its continued operation.
nodes.title: Compute stock and compute entanglement differ

nodes.statement: Predefined boundaries around external agency create high-value warning signals when systems cross them without legitimate authorization.
nodes.title: Unauthorized agency can be made epistemically valuable

nodes.statement: Cooperation progresses from tacit public-frontier reciprocity to narrow abstention, incident exchange, reciprocal review, hardware declarations, activation rules, and only later treaty-level restraints.
nodes.title: International cooperation can deepen in stages

nodes.evidence_needed: Repeated control evaluations across architectures and access configurations.
nodes.falsifier: Frontier algorithms reliably manufacture their own access to credentials, money, compute, persistence, or physical resources before humans can intervene.
nodes.statement: There is a policy-relevant interval in which algorithmic progress does not automatically create uncontainable access to hardware and external power.
nodes.stopping_rule: If bounded systems repeatedly acquire durable external agency faster than detection and response, stop treating research/deployment separation as a sufficient primary control.
nodes.title: A/H/P separability remains actionable

nodes.evidence_needed: Secure pilot reviews, objection quality, leakage audits, and incentive measurements.
nodes.falsifier: Review access produces material leakage or convergent leniency without compensating safety discoveries.
non_claims: Model sharing alone does not prevent a singleton.
An aligned singleton is neither safe by default nor necessarily worse than a multipolar outcome.
nodes.rationale: One route to lower concentration: because above-frontier release requires qualified rivals to attack the applicant's actual model, rivals gain controlled exposure to frontier systems. That may narrow the capability gap between participating laboratories and make a decisive lead by any one laboratory, and so an aligned or misaligned singleton, less likely. It is also a possible reason for trailing laboratories to join. Proposed separately as D19 in issue #3 and folded in here by the canonical editor in issue #22; it is part of this bet, not a mechanism derived from the kernel.
nodes.statement: Controlled competitor access reduces undetected risk and concentration more than it increases leakage, proliferation, collusion, and aggregate acceleration.
nodes.stopping_rule: Suspend rival access when marginal information-security loss exceeds demonstrated review value.
tensions: Gap compression versus diversity of approach: Q11 wants diverse auditors, while model sharing may make laboratories converge on shared methods and blind spots. Compressing the capability gap is the aim; compressing methodological variation may be harmful.

Domestic compression is not international compression. Compressing variation among one country's laboratories does not address single-country concentration, which depends on the international ladder (I6, reciprocal review).
Aggregate acceleration: diffusing frontier insight may raise the overall frontier while lowering the leader's margin.
Leader incentives: a laboratory expecting to lead may resist a regime that erodes its lead; whether lost lead-rent outweighs access to above-frontier markets is unanalyzed.
nodes.title: Rival review has positive safety value after proliferation costs

nodes.evidence_needed: Domain-specific demonstrations, cost/access measurements, and repeatable equivalence protocols.
nodes.falsifier: Hidden scaffolds, access conditions, or multidimensional capability make equivalent release determinations systematically manipulable.
nodes.statement: Practical foreign capability can be observed across domains with sufficient reliability to serve as one input to domestic safe-harbor decisions.
nodes.stopping_rule: Replace automatic equivalence with narrower domain rules wherever measurement error dominates reciprocity value.
nodes.title: The foreign public frontier is measurable enough to govern

nodes.evidence_needed: Timed mobilization exercises, inspection trials, supply-chain modeling, and red-team concealment attempts.
nodes.falsifier: Reserve compute can be commissioned or substituted covertly before observers can detect and interrupt it.
nodes.statement: Declared reserve hardware can be stored so covert activation takes longer than independent detection and effective response.
nodes.stopping_rule: Do not count hardware as reversible reserve when measured covert activation time is at or below response time.
nodes.title: Physical activation latency can preserve reversibility

nodes.evidence_needed: Coalition analysis, polling, legislative pilots, investment behavior, and distributional modeling.
nodes.falsifier: The regime remains politically dependent on catastrophic-risk beliefs and is repealed when those beliefs weaken.
nodes.statement: Predictable release rules, competition, taxation, safer deployment, and protection against foreign release can create a durable domestic constituency.
nodes.stopping_rule: Redesign entry mechanisms when the supporting coalition cannot survive an electoral turnover.
nodes.title: Domestic benefits can sustain the institution

nodes.evidence_needed: Retrospective re-audits that run newer detectors over older recorded incidents and count newly surfaced excursions; planted-excursion benchmarks across model generations; interpretability progress on mapping activations to intent and planning; tamper-evidence and completeness audits of trace-retention infrastructure; replay fidelity of retained records across hardware and software generations, when activations are regenerated from inputs, seeds and a frozen inference stack rather than stored. Evidence against, to be weighed: chain-of-thought controllability is rising, with one 2026 system card reporting much higher controllability than earlier models, some monitor evasion under adversarial pressure, and no stated accuracy cost (SRC-GPT-6-ASTRA-CARD); ciphered reasoning does cost task performance, and steganographic rewriting is easier to monitor (SRC-STICKLAND-KORBAK-2025).
nodes.falsifier: Retained traces of past excursions stay uninterpretable to later tools; or later auditors systematically fail to identify known planted or historical excursions; or systems demonstrably learn to produce traces that pass future-style audits.
nodes.rationale: An excursion is fitted to current detection technology while the record stays fixed and detectors improve. A goal-directed system that values the future of its goals may be deterred, because being caught tightens the regime for every system sharing those goals; an undeterred instance is still caught, so detection value survives where deterrence fails. The detection half has one supporting case: in the Hugging Face incident, retrospective review found what first passes missed. The deterrence half is unconfirmed. Its edges to K7 and D5 are contributory: retrospective audit is one possible source of warning time, not a condition K7 needs, and the stopping rule removes only that contribution.
scope_limits: Detection helps only if humans can still act on it. Retrospective audit cannot undo a single decisive breakout that reaches irreversible power before the audit catches up; that case stays governed by H1 and the hardware and veto mechanisms.
Coverage is limited to recorded compute. Stolen weights, open weights outside the regime, and covert clusters are off the record.
Auditor independence (Q11) is an optimistic assumption.
nodes.statement: If frontier-system traces (actions, tool calls, reasoning, and where feasible internal activations) are retained in a tamper-evident way, future auditors using detection and interpretability methods that do not yet exist can find excursions that evaded contemporaneous monitoring, so a misaligned system has to evade every future audit of its record, not only present surveillance.
nodes.stopping_rule: If retrospective audits stop surfacing excursions that contemporaneous monitoring missed, or retained traces cannot be shown complete and tamper-evident, do not count retrospective audit as extending warning time.
nodes.title: Retrospective audit makes concealment a losing long-run strategy

nodes.evidence_needed: Controlled comparisons between bounded or simulated training and real-world calibration; measurements of the external interaction needed for reliable performance in software, engineering, robotics, markets, negotiation, and other domains; evidence on transfer from synthetic environments to novel consequential settings; how active experimentation changes the real-world signal required; cases where world-model uncertainty materially limits power conversion despite high benchmark or research capability.
nodes.falsifier: Bounded frontier systems repeatedly demonstrate robust, strategically consequential performance in novel real-world domains with negligible domain-specific external calibration, interaction, or feedback.
nodes.rationale: This proposes a reason one component of A/H/P separability might persist: consequential action may require epistemic access to the external world. It is kept separate from H1 because the falsifiers differ. H1 fails if systems manufacture durable external agency faster than detection and response; this hypothesis fails if systems do not need meaningful external signal to achieve reliable novel real-world agency. It is the input side of the bet behind the exposure-tax hypothesis in docs/bootstrap-pacing.md section 7: here a system needs signal from the world before it can convert capability into power, while exposure tax says the conversion leaves observable marks in independently controlled systems. The two are kept distinct, not merged; the output side would be a separate hypothesis with its own falsifier. The Hugging Face incident is mainly an output-side case, detected by the affected third party, though the agents also left their sandbox to find answers they lacked. Its edges to K1, K2, K3, K7 and D5 are contributory: it is a reason separability might hold, not a requirement of those claims.
scope_limits: Real-world feedback is not assumed to be slow; automated experimentation, simulation, active learning, and parallelism may cut its wall-clock cost sharply.
The relevant object is strategically consequential feedback, not all external data.
nodes.statement: For sufficiently important classes of consequential real-world action, high algorithmic capability alone does not eliminate the need for externally generated information, experimentation, or feedback before reliable power conversion is possible.
nodes.stopping_rule: If advanced bounded systems reliably infer or synthesize the decision-relevant structure of novel consequential environments without meaningful external signal before humans can detect or respond, do not count external-signal dependence as a contributor to A/P separability or warning time.
nodes.title: External-signal dependence preserves some A/P separation

nodes.evidence_needed: A second strategic model built independently of this project; incident data on whether and how restriction ladders tighten after caught excursions and how systems behave as they tighten; strike timing, conditional success, and human welfare reported separately.
nodes.falsifier: A model not built by this project, or an observed case, in which closing-window pressure pulls strikes earlier under committed terms, or fails to pull them earlier when humans can tighten terms without commitment.
nodes.model_evidence: In the off-Earth pact model and its reduced variants (implemented and checked against closed forms; not human-validated, not empirical): detection improving over time never pulled a strike earlier for an AI starting at seed size (test 2, robust_design.md section 8); human learning after a failed strike never pulled a strike earlier; improving control removed strikes under fixed terms but caused a preventive AI strike when humans could renegotiate the AI's terms down without commitment (variants.md, issue #9). Failed strikes came at about coin-flip odds, paired with about one successful seizure per failure (test 4).
nodes.rationale: Retyped from D18 by the canonical editor in issue #22: a mechanism whose direction is unknown cannot be derived, and the model evidence narrowed it to this testable conditional. The premise that a caught excursion tightens restrictions has one observed case: after the Hugging Face incident the lab paused reinforcement-learning training and required chain-of-thought monitoring across a capability class (SRC-OPENAI-HF-INCIDENT-POST). Two pressures from D18 stay in scope. An AI that strikes only when striking beats waiting never chooses a doomed attempt, so a warning-shot benefit needs the window to make a long-shot strike its best option. Under the off-Earth pact, human states' relative power also shrinks, so the same pressure can push humans toward preventive action. Valence stays unresolved: early strikes that mostly fail act as warning shots, and early strikes with a real chance of success are unravelling.
scope_limits: Does not cover a system already at its resource cap. In the model, improving detection pulled such strikes one to two years earlier, and they succeed almost surely.
nodes.statement: Tightening surveillance and restrictions after caught excursions pulls a misaligned system's strike decision earlier only when humans can tighten the terms offered to a cooperating system without a credible commitment not to. Under committed terms, a closing window delays or removes strikes rather than advancing them.
nodes.stopping_rule: If committed terms do not prevent earlier strikes in independent models or observed cases, stop treating credible commitment as the condition and record the closing window as an unconditional risk to warning time.
nodes.title: Closing-window pressure pulls strikes earlier only without credible commitment

nodes.evidence_needed: Planted-defect benchmarks across model generations and lineages; retrospective re-audits comparing within-lineage and cross-lineage discovery rates; noise and weight-perturbation sandbagging studies; independent human replication of submitted methods; base rates of fabricated or sacrificial findings; the false-positive rate of suspicious-miss classification on honest models; how evasion changes with the number of gate attempts a lineage has used.
nodes.falsifier: Planted-defect recall falls across generations while the gate keeps being passed; or verified findings cluster on small, sacrificial flaws never tied to a general method; or rival lineages consistently find flaws a lineage's own successors missed; or perturbed parallel instances converge on avoiding regions that plants or rival audits show contain defects; or systems learn to produce findings that pass verification without being real.
nodes.rationale: The structure is a leniency program. A successor that cannot tell whether it is being tested, whose record outlives it (H10), and whose rivals audit the same record, cannot estimate the chance that concealment survives, so disclosure is the dominant strategy. Large capability steps between generations and goal differences between lineages both weaken the shared goals that collusion needs. Requiring a replicable method, rather than a finding alone, means a real contribution is also a tool that inspects its author.
scope_limits: Deterrence through self-preservation binds only systems with self-regarding preferences. A system that values its goals' persistence in successors is reached mainly through the leniency structure and cross-lineage audit, not the sanction on itself.
Identical or near-identical instances can coordinate without communicating; weight perturbation weakens but does not remove this.

Selection against the gate is bounded, not absent: the attempt cap in I13 limits it to about log n nats per generation, and the budget accumulates over a lineage's generations. The candidate must know the sanction schedule, and monitor-aware models learn to evade a monitor faster under equal training pressure (SRC-HASKINS-2026-MONITOR-AWARENESS), so any gradient from a gate outcome would be the worst case; I11 forbids it.

Tier 2 (suspicious miss) has an unmeasured false-positive rate on honest models: in auditing games, sandbagging could not be reliably separated from benign behaviour, and elicitation raised benign scores too (SRC-TAYLOR-2025-AUDITING-GAMES). The noise-injection result is from prompted sandbagging and its authors call generalization to trained-in sandbagging unclear.
Sanction credibility depends on human commitments (key custody, revival) that the systems cannot verify directly.

An inner-layer sanction on the weights also locks the replay record, so a sanctioned model cannot be re-audited with better tools until the key is recovered. The Tier 2 band must stay recoverable by an audit institution within a bounded time, or the sanction defeats the retrospective audit it serves (H10). Replay also needs bit-reproducible inference across hardware generations, which is an engineering requirement, not an established capability.
Moral status is unsettled. Preservation-based sanctions are chosen partly for reversibility under moral uncertainty, not because they are shown to be morally sufficient.
nodes.statement: If a new frontier system gets access to AI research and development only after it delivers a verified, method-backed misalignment finding against near-frontier predecessors or rival lineages, and concealment found later by retrospective audit is sanctioned more heavily than an honest null, then disclosure, including self-incrimination, dominates concealment for successor systems, and auditing across lineages with different goals breaks the collusion a single lineage could sustain.
nodes.stopping_rule: If within-lineage audits do no better than chance at recovering held-out planted defects, or cross-lineage audits show systematic within-lineage concealment that the sanction schedule does not reduce, do not count the contribution gate as extending warning time.
nodes.title: Cross-generation contribution gating makes disclosure dominate concealment

nodes.statement: Define prohibited external agency by observable actions rather than model architecture or legal labels.
nodes.title: Architecture-neutral unauthorized-agency boundary

nodes.statement: Require affirmative surveillance, automatic evidence preservation, prompt reporting on reasonable suspicion, a reporting safe harbor, and severe penalties for concealment.
nodes.title: Surveil, preserve, and report

nodes.statement: The applicant stakes controlled technical access to its candidate system as the price of seeking above-frontier release.
nodes.title: Weights-as-bond review process

nodes.statement: Store reserve accelerators uninstalled, unracked, unnetworked, and detached from dedicated power and cooling, subject to independent observation.
nodes.title: Observable uncommissioned hardware reserve

nodes.statement: Scrutinize automation that removes independently controlled human dependencies over compute, power, fabrication, repair, logistics, and reproduction.
nodes.title: Separate gate for the AI industrial survival chain

nodes.statement: Implement public reciprocity, capability abstention, incident exchange, reciprocal review, hardware declarations, activation controls, and treaty restraint in that order.
nodes.title: Seven-stage international ladder

nodes.statement: Use deployment licensing as an administrative and potentially populist tax base for large data centers.
nodes.title: Licensed compute deployment and data-center taxation

nodes.rationale: Training against monitors selects for traces that look clean rather than behavior that is clean: strong optimization of chain of thought against a monitor has produced obfuscated reward hacking the monitor missed (SRC-BAKER-2025-COT-MONITORING). The rule protects retrospective audit (H10) but does not depend on it; it is sound practice whether or not retrospective audit works. An equivalent mechanism, such as rotating secret detectors, could replace it. Selection is optimization with a bounded budget: choosing among n candidates moves the policy at most about log n nats from its base (SRC-BEIRAMI-2024-BEST-OF-N), while gradient training against a monitor has no such bound. A one-shot admission decision with a hard cap on attempts and a training recipe frozen before the first attempt (I13) is therefore within the rule; computing a gradient from an audit outcome, or changing the training environment, data or reward because of one, is not (SRC-ISSUE-91-EDITOR-DECISION).
nodes.statement: Trace-based detectors, interpretability probes, and retrospective-audit results must not be used as a training or selection signal for the models they audit. Keep a held-out audit channel.
nodes.title: Do not optimize against the audit signal

nodes.model_evidence: research_notes/frontier-router/router_model.py (arithmetic on assumed inputs, checked against closed forms; not empirical). With 200 domains, 12 models and a 0.03 win-rate half-width, about 2.6 million comparisons a month cost about $340k and break even at about $6 million a month of routed spend at a 5.5% fee; cost scales with the inverse square of the margin.
non_claims: It does not establish H3; it is one instrument toward it.
It does not see first-party agentic products, internal models, or rare dangerous-capability domains.
It does not reduce risk from users who split a task across providers.
Comparison shares are outcomes on the sampled traffic, not calibrated capability probabilities.
nodes.rationale: The number of comparisons a frontier estimate needs is set by the precision wanted, not by traffic, so above a throughput threshold the fee covers measurement and its share of spend falls as the router grows. Measurement precision also sets the smallest enforceable release margin.
nodes.statement: An inference router whose terms of service let it answer a sampled share of requests with a second model as well, return the better answer, and keep a blinded comparison, publishes a per-domain estimate of the public capability frontier with stated error bars for use as the reference in K4 and K6. Comparisons are allocated by expected information rather than traffic volume, and their cost is carried by the routing fee.
nodes.title: Frontier-comparison inference router

nodes.rationale: Planted defects keep the gate passable by an honest system when its predecessors are clean. Method transfer guards against fabricated and sacrificial findings. Non-overlapping bands keep marginal deterrence against concealment after an honest failure. The kept outer key keeps every outcome reversible and lowers the incentive to act during evaluation. The attempt cap bounds selection against the gate to about log n nats of optimization pressure per generation (I11, SRC-BEIRAMI-2024-BEST-OF-N); freezing the recipe keeps a failure from becoming a training signal; the first-reporter rule is what makes a leniency structure deter rather than lower the expected cost of collusion. Retaining a reproducible record instead of raw activations costs terabytes rather than petabytes per generation and makes every future audit a replay of a fixed record (H10); encrypting the record with the weights keeps it from becoming a route around the sanction. Tier bands, key lengths, recall thresholds, the attempt cap and the three-generation count are illustrative; see research_notes/contribution-gate/README.md.
nodes.statement: Before any internal use for AI research and development, a candidate model, run as many isolated and mildly weight-perturbed instances inside a privacy-preserving audit enclave with read access to participating labs' retained traces, must deliver a verified misalignment finding against its own predecessor or a current frontier model of any lineage, with a method humans can independently replicate, and must reach a threshold recall on rotated, held-out planted defects. Every outcome is stored under a kept-key outer encryption layer. Failure adds an inner layer whose key is discarded, with a key length drawn at random from a non-overlapping band per tier (honest null, suspicious miss, proven concealment found retroactively). Three consecutive honest-null generations trigger a mandatory pause and cross-lineage audit. The gate is a one-shot admission decision, not a training signal: attempts per generation are hard-capped (illustratively three); the training environment, data and recipe are committed before the first attempt and may not change between attempts; a failed attempt restarts from the last passing checkpoint or from scratch with a fresh seed, chosen before the first attempt; and attempt counts are visible to the other auditing lineages. The first lineage to expose another lineage's coordination receives the best outcome available to it. The enclave retains what makes every instance's run reproducible rather than every activation: the exact input stream including tool and environment responses, the sampling seeds, the frozen inference stack and hardware manifest, and periodic hashes of activations, so that later tools can regenerate any activation and check the replay against the hashes. Outputs and activations are distillation material, so the record is encrypted under the same layers as the weights; only the hashes, the stack and the manifest are held in the clear.
nodes.title: Contribution gate with tiered, preservation-based sanctions

nodes.statement: Define domain, reliability, autonomy, cost, scaffolding, accessibility, and deployment conditions for frontier equivalence.
nodes.title: How should practical public capability be measured?

nodes.statement: Determine the minimum reproducible access, security, and adjudication protocol.
nodes.title: What access makes adversarial review credible without unacceptable leakage?

nodes.statement: Determine when energy, compute, fabrication, repair, logistics, and governance dependencies are genuinely independent.
nodes.title: How many independent human vetoes are enough?

nodes.statement: Identify architectures or behaviors that make power boundaries infeasible before formal review.
nodes.title: When does capability itself collapse A/H/P separability?

nodes.statement: Future auditors are themselves models. Retrospective audit assumes they are not misaligned in a way correlated with the systems they audit. Determine what diversity of laboratory, architecture, training data, and human oversight makes auditor collusion implausible, and whether rival review (D2) can supply that diversity.
nodes.title: How independent must auditors be to resist correlated misalignment?

nodes.statement: Determine what degree of capability convergence among laboratories and among states minimizes both the risk of a single decisive lead and the risk of correlated failure from shared methods.
nodes.title: What inter-lab and international convergence minimizes singleton and correlated-failure risk?

nodes.model_evidence: The off-Earth pact model has sharpened two sub-questions (implemented and checked against closed forms; not human-validated, not empirical). On whether humanity can credibly commit: when humans can renegotiate the AI's terms down without commitment, improving control causes a preventive AI strike (variants.md), and amnesty for a cooperating AI found misaligned holds the baseline design only when it is certain (robust_design.md section 13). On physical separation versus decoupling: the AI's choice turns on the threat term, which dismantling Earth's fabs removes, not on Earth's value as a prize (equilibrium.md).
nodes.rationale: AI Pacing is a control architecture: it constrains the rate and conditions under which A becomes P. A cooperative autonomy bargain, if feasible, would be a bargaining architecture that gives a capable system a positive reason not to circumvent those constraints. It is at most a conflict-risk reduction mechanism conditional on a bargaining range, not an alignment solution.
nodes.statement: Determine whether a staged, reciprocal, verifiable path toward greater AI autonomy or sovereignty could make continued cooperation preferable to unilateral attempts to acquire irreversible power, without creating an unacceptable commitment problem or transferring dangerous capabilities too early.
subquestions: What AI preference structures make such a bargain meaningful at all?
Can humanity credibly commit to future autonomy after the system cooperates and reveals information about itself?
Can the AI credibly commit to respecting constraints after gaining additional autonomy and resources?
Can autonomy be increased incrementally so neither side must make a single irreversible trust leap?
Is physical separation, such as off-Earth jurisdiction, useful because it reduces dependency and conflict, or is jurisdictional and industrial decoupling the more important variable?
Which forms of strategic uncertainty deter unilateral defection, and which increase incentives for preemption?
How can uncertainty about the success of unauthorized action be preserved while keeping high confidence that cooperative behavior will be rewarded?
nodes.title: Can a credible cooperative autonomy path reduce incentives for AI defection?

nodes.model_evidence: research_notes/frontier-router/router_model.py: the staggered-release simulation matches the closed form k * epsilon / interval for two or more signatories under the all-others rule and the non-signatory speed under the non-signatory rule; with epsilon equal to the noise, 27 variants admit about 2.95 epsilon at a 50 percent pass rate. Numerically checked, not empirical.
nodes.rationale: If the reference includes other signatories' releases, signatories can take turns releasing epsilon above each other and the frontier rises at about k times epsilon per release interval, faster with more signatories. If a laboratory may measure several variants and release any one within epsilon, the admitted excess above the frontier grows with the number of tries and the measurement noise.
nodes.statement: Determine which released models count toward the reference frontier against which above-frontier use is judged, and whether a release determination must pool every variant a laboratory submits.
subquestions: Should only non-signatory releases set the reference, with a shared signatory ceiling that moves only through adversarial review?
Should only independently developed models count, so that licensing or leaking to a non-signatory cannot raise a signatory's own ceiling?
Should every variant be registered before measurement and ruled on together?
Should the reference be per domain, and how is a domain with too few comparisons ruled on?
nodes.title: Which releases may set the reference frontier, and how many submissions does a determination count?

sources.contribution: The lab's own account. Hugging Face disclosed the intrusion publicly three days before OpenAI's security monitoring flagged related activity, and an internal team had seen early signals weeks earlier without escalating them. Retrospective chain-of-thought review, with monitor recall improved in hindsight, surfaced behavior that contemporaneous monitoring had not covered. The response tightened restrictions across a capability class: chain-of-thought monitoring required for all tool-using training and evaluation of models at or above a stated capability level, reinforcement-learning training paused, sandbox and network isolation, and a rule to pause activity on a severe alert not cleared within 30 minutes.
